text.en:
1. (1) This Act may be cited as the BERNAMA Act 1967.

(2) This Act applies throughout Malaysia.

Interpretation

2. In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires—

"BERNAMA" means the Pertubuhan Berita Nasional Malaysia

as established under subsection 3(1);

"Board" means the Board of Governors of BERNAMA appointed

under section 7;

"news or news material" includes international, regional and

national—

(a) news;

(b) photographs;

(c) information;

(d) features; and

(e) economic, commodity and financial data,

in whatever form or manner.

Part II

ESTABLISHMENT OF BERNAMA,

ITS POWERS AND OBJECTS

Establishment of BERNAMA and its powers

3. (1) A body corporate by the name of "Pertubuhan Berita

Nasional Malaysia", or in English the "Malaysian National News

Agency", is established with perpetual succession and a common

seal.

(2) BERNAMA shall, in respect of movable or immovable

property, have the power—

(a) to acquire and hold such movable or immovable property;

and

(b) to dispose of, or otherwise deal with, such movable or

immovable property.

(3) Without prejudice to the generality of subsection (2) but

subject to the Federal Constitution and this Act, BERNAMA

shall have and exercise all the powers that may be necessary or

expedient for the attainment of its objects or any of the objects.

(4) BERNAMA may at its discretion arrange at an appropriate

time for the reception through subscription, payment, exchange

or other means of international, regional and other news or news

material and the distribution of the news or news material to

subscribers on such terms as may be arranged.
BERNAMA 7

Common seal

4. (1) BERNAMA shall have a common seal and the seal may

be broken, changed, altered or made anew as BERNAMA deems

fit.

(2) Until a seal is provided under this section, a stamp bearing

the inscription "Pertubuhan Berita Nasional Malaysia" may be

used as the common seal of BERNAMA.

(3) All deeds, documents and other instruments requiring the

seal of BERNAMA shall be sealed accordingly in the presence

of two members of the Board who shall sign every such deed,

document or instrument to which such seal is affixed.

(4) Such signing shall without further attestation be sufficient

evidence that the seal was duly and properly affixed and is the

lawful seal of BERNAMA.

Power to enter into any arrangement for sharing of profits, etc.

5. BERNAMA, with the approval of the Minister and the

concurrence of the Minister of Finance, may—

(a) enter into any arrangement for sharing of profits, union of

interests, co-operation or joint venture with any person

or body of persons; or

(b) establish or promote the establishment and expansion of

companies under the Companies Act 1965 [Act 125].

Objects of BERNAMA

6. The objects of BERNAMA are—

(a) to seek for and present complete, objective and impartial

news or news material on any matter of public and

national interests within and outside Malaysia;

(b) to distribute such news or news material to subscribers

on payment either in the form of fees or news exchange

or both; and

(c) to report truthfully and fairly, without prejudice to public

and national interest, the views of all sections of the

population of Malaysia.

Part III

BOARD OF GOVERNORS

Constitution of Board of Governors

7. (1) The management of BERNAMA is vested in a Board of

Governors which shall comprise not less than eleven and not

more than thirteen members appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan

Agong.

(2) The Board shall consist of the following members who are

citizens of Malaysia:

(a) a Chairman;

(b) not more than six representatives of the Government of

Malaysia; and

(c) not more than six representatives of proprietors of newspapers

in Malaysia who are subscribers to BERNAMA.

(3) The number of representatives appointed under

paragraphs (2)(b) and (c) shall be of equal proportion.

(4) The Chairman of the Board shall be appointed after

consultations with the proprietors of newspapers in Malaysia who

are subscribers to BERNAMA.

(5) The members of the Board referred to in paragraph (2)(c)

shall be appointed from amongst persons nominated by the

proprietors of newspapers in Malaysia who are subscribers to

BERNAMA.

(6) Part I of the Schedule shall apply to the members of the

Board.
BERNAMA 9

Functions of the Board

8. The Board shall be responsible for carrying out the objects of

BERNAMA as set out in section 6 and to formulate the general

policy of BERNAMA.

Part IV

SUPERVISORY COUNCIL

Establishment of Supervisory Council

9. A Supervisory Council is established.

Functions of Supervisory Council

10. The Supervisory Council shall have the following functions:

(a) to ensure that BERNAMA shall at all times abide by this

Act;

(b) to consider any complaint from a newspaper, radio or

television subscriber to BERNAMA alleging failure or

default by BERNAMA to comply with any of the objects

or principles laid down in this Act; and

(c) to consider any matter referred to it by the Board.

Members of Supervisory Council

11. (1) The Supervisory Council shall comprise the following

members who shall be appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong:

(a) a Judge of the High Court who shall be the President of

the Council;

(b) one representative of the Government of Malaysia;

(c) one representative of the newspapers in Malaysia;

(d) the Vice-Chancellor of any one of the Universities in

Malaysia; and

(e) one other person.

(2) The member referred to in paragraph (1)(a) shall be appointed

in consultation with the Chief Justice.

(3) Part II of the Schedule shall apply to the members of the

Supervisory Council.

Inquiries by Supervisory Council

12. (1) The Supervisory Council shall hold an inquiry into—

(a) any complaint under paragraph 10(b); or

(b) any matter referred to it by the Board under paragraph 10(c).

(2) For the purposes of an inquiry under this section, the

Supervisory Council may—

(a) receive evidence orally or in writing; or

(b) require any person to give such information,

which in its opinion is necessary for the purpose of making a

finding.

(3) The Supervisory Council shall deliver its findings and any

recommendations as it deems fit in writing to the Board as soon

as possible upon the conclusion of the inquiry.

(4) The findings and recommendations, if any, of the Supervisory

Council shall, if so directed by the Supervisory Council, be

published in full by the Board.

Part V

GENERAL

Appointment of officers and servants

13. (1) The Board shall appoint a General Manager, a Secretary

to the Board and such other officers and servants as may be

necessary for carrying out its functions under this Act.
BERNAMA 11

(2) The General Manager, the Secretary to the Board and other

officers and servants of the Board shall be engaged on such terms

and conditions as may be prescribed by the Board.

General Manager

14. (1) The General Manager shall be the chief executive officer

of BERNAMA who is responsible to the Board.

(2) All officers and servants of the Board shall be under the

control of the General Manager.

Powers of Board to accept grants, etc.

15. The Board may accept any contributions, grants, endowments,

gifts or bequests made to or in favour of BERNAMA.

Powers of Board to borrow

16. The Board may, subject to the approval of the Treasury,

borrow or secure the payment of any money required by the

Board for the proper carrying out of its functions under this Act.

Investments

17. (1) The assets of BERNAMA may be invested by the Board

in investments authorized by law for the investment of trust funds.

(2) Notwithstanding subsection (1), the Board shall not make

any investment in securities issued or registered or other properties

situated outside Malaysia except with the approval of the Minister

of Finance.

Accounts and audit

18. (1) The Board shall keep proper accounts and other records

in respect of its operations.

(2) The accounts of BERNAMA shall be audited by an auditor

appointed by the Board with the approval of the Minister.

(3) The Board shall, as soon as may be after the end of each

calendar year, submit to the Minister an audited account of the

income and expenditure of the Board for that year together with

a statement of its assets and liabilities.

(4) The Minister shall cause the account and statement submitted

under subsection (3) together with a copy of any observations of

the auditor thereon to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.

Delegation by the Board

19. (1) The Board may delegate, in writing under its common

seal, to any person or body any of its duties as may be necessary

to be performed in or outside Malaysia.

(2) Any person or body delegated with such duties under

subsection (1) shall—

(a) have no control over the moneys of BERNAMA; and

(b) act in all respects in accordance with the discretion of

the Board.

Board may establish committees

20. (1) The Board may establish committees to consider special

questions as may be referred to the committees by the Board.

(2) The committees shall perform its functions according to

the directions given to the committees by the Board.

Subscribers

21. The following classes of subscribers are entitled to enter

into arrangements to have the services of BERNAMA:

(a) newspapers operating in Malaysia; and

(b) any other newspapers, news agencies, institutions, bodies

or persons and any other subscribers as may be authorized

by the Board.
BERNAMA 13

Income of BERNAMA

22. (1) The income of BERNAMA shall consist of subscriptions

and contributions, grants, endowments, gifts or bequests as may

be made to or in favour of BERNAMA.

(2) The income of BERNAMA shall be applied solely for the

following purposes:

(a) to promote the objects of BERNAMA;

(b) to pay remuneration, pension, superannuation, allowances

and any provident fund scheme to any officer or servant

employed or engaged under this Act; or

(c) to pay any expenses incurred in pursuance of this Act.

(3) No portion of the income of BERNAMA shall be paid or

transferred, directly or indirectly, by way of dividend, bonus or

otherwise by way of profit to any person.

Offices of BERNAMA

23. BERNAMA shall have a principal office in Malaysia and may

establish such other office at such place in or outside Malaysia

as the Board may determine.

Language of BERNAMA

24. The working languages of BERNAMA are the national

language and the English language.

Guarantee of full service

25. (1) Notwithstanding any arrangements which BERNAMA

may enter into for the reception and distribution of international

news, subscribers to BERNAMA shall be guaranteed the right, on

request and on terms in regard to payment to be decided by the

Board, to receive through BERNAMA the full service supplied

to BERNAMA by any international news agency.

(2) Arrangements for news collection and distribution made

by BERNAMA shall be without prejudice to the right of the

newspapers who are subscribers to BERNAMA to make their

own independent arrangements for news coverage by their own

correspondents.

(3) In subsection (2), "correspondents" include editorial staff

of a newspaper and any person who writes or supplies news for

a fee either as a part-time or full-time occupation.

Protection against liability of members of Board and Supervisory

Council

26. No member of the Board or of the Supervisory Council shall

incur any personal liability for any loss or damage caused by any

act or omission in the management or conduct of the affairs of

the Board or the Supervisory Council unless such loss or damage

is occasioned by an intentionally wrongful act or omission on

his part.
